category_title: Adolescent with emotional/behavioral disorder and academic frustration
minimal_context: Isaac is participating in a morning check-in with his teacher to review his planner and turn in his homework.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Good morning, Isaac. It is time for our morning check-in. Please take out your planner and hand in last night's homework.

STUDENT: I don't have it. I didn't even know what assignment was due.

TUTOR: You need to keep track of your assignments. Look in your backpack and see what materials you brought for class today.

STUDENT: (Digs through his bag) I don't have my materials. I think I actually completed the assignment, but I can't find it anywhere in here.

TUTOR: If you cannot find your work, you will have to sit down and redo the assignment right now.

STUDENT: No! I'm not doing it again! (Pushes his desk away and refuses to open his book)

options.A: Provide Isaac with a sectioned binder to organize completed assignments, incomplete assignments, and class notes, and teach him daily to use his planner to record assignments and due dates.
options.B: Guide Isaac through a healing-lake visualization, encouraging him to carefully observe the lake and notice that it is always changing, yet always itself, during the morning check-in.
options.C: Implement relatively tight timelines for Isaac to complete his homework assignments, organize his materials, and prepare for the daily morning check-in with the teacher.
options.D: Address Isaac's feelings mutually rather than repressing them, allowing for the exploration of his disappointments and constraints regarding his missing assignments and disorganized materials.
